flakes.signature: The harness refused a tool call the fake model made
flakes.cause: A race in the product, not a flake of the fake model's. Novadeck started a briefed Antigravity worker as `agy -i "<line>"`, whose first request goes within a second of its start, and Antigravity takes a turn's MCP tools only as the turn starts: when Novadeck's MCP server hadn't listed its tools yet, as on a loaded macOS runner (over 1 s), the whole first turn went without them (owl's requests in both traces had no <mcp_servers> and no call_mcp_tool), so the fake model's agents call, named from another terminal's request, was an unknown tool. Reproduced on Linux with the MCP launcher slowed by 0.1 s or more; probed on 1.4.12 and 1.5.1 that a later-listed server never joins the running turn. Fixed: Antigravity always starts plain, and the doorbell rings it only once a terminal's MCP session has listed Novadeck's tools (10 s at most); tasks.e2e.ts checks every harness's task turn has the tools with the server started 2 s late.

flakes.test: src/pty/native.test.ts > installed native PTY dependency > keeps repeated child sessions alive for multiple writes and their natural exit
flakes.signature: Timed out waiting for PTY \d+ (?:exit|output NATIVE_SESSION_)
flakes.cause: Input stalls under CI load, on both of Windows' ConPTYs; measured in #720. On a quiet runner a 65-char line reaches the child in 8 ms on the system ConPTY and 3 ms on the bundled one (2801 chars: about 0.2 s and 0.09 s, growing with length, which fits libuv reading one console record per call). On a busy one, as the relay's Rust tests run alongside, each line was held 2 s on the bundled ConPTY, and 3 to 10 s or more on the system one in the seven failures, while output came back within a millisecond. The test ran on the system ConPTY until #720, which moved it to the bundled one spawnPty uses (and pinned that in a pty test) and gave each Windows step 30 s instead of 10 and the test 120 s. A stall longer than that would still fail, so it stays known. #722 found a separate 3 s at each start, the bundled console host waiting for an answer to its device attributes request, which the test now gives. That isn't these stalls: the system ConPTY, which makes no such request, stalled too, and without the wait the test took 36 to 37 s in the busy job and 920 ms on a quiet runner, where the answer changed nothing. That's above the 13.5 to 27.7 s it took net of the wait before; why isn't measured, though the steps may now fall inside the relay's busy window, where the wait spread them out.

flakes.test: src/engines/server.test.ts > a server > starts again on another port when something takes the one it was given
flakes.signature: AssertionError: expected 2 to be 3
flakes.cause: The test's own: of the three ports it expects to be different, two were the same. Its first two starts only say their port is taken and exit (losesPort), holding no socket, on purpose, so as not to race other test workers for free ports. The server's next pick (freePort in backend/runner/src/engines/server.ts: bind port 0, then close) can then get the same port back from the OS. The server promises no more: a port another process really holds can't be picked again while it's held. A fix would hold each lost port in the test, bringing back the race its comment avoids, or let the test choose the ports.

flakes.signature: Test timed out in 60000ms
flakes.cause: Unknown, seen once. A timeout here means the test's real check passed: its budget is 15 s of CPU, and the 60 s timeout only bounds the wall clock, so a real blow-up fails with `expected N to be less than 15000`, which this doesn't excuse. The test took 68 s of wall clock, against 2.1 s, 28.8 s and 31.1 s on earlier passing macOS runs, so about half the limit on two of those three. Its comment's "about 1 s" is a CPU figure, so these don't compare with it. Why hex takes so much longer than the other shapes in the same job (24 s for base64, 5 to 8 s for the rest) hasn't been looked into; it runs first, beside other packages' tests.

flakes.test: src/pty/follow.test.ts > a hangup followed through an agent > wakes an agent stopped on its way out as soon as the shell has gone
flakes.signature: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '[^']*terminal-follow-[^']*/saved'
flakes.cause: The test read the woken agent's 'saved' file the moment `end()` returned, which on a slow macOS runner can come before the agent has written it (ENOENT at about 5.4 s). Fixed by task/ci-flakes: the test waits up to 3 s for the file, then checks it and the 4 s bound, and runs on macOS again (the skip from #785 is gone). If it returns, the agent was really stopped and never woken.

flakes.test: src/client.test.ts > runner client over WebSocket > resynchronizes a slow viewer with a fresh snapshot instead of failing
flakes.signature: WireError: CONTROL_REQUIRED
flakes.cause: The test wrote 21 lines through the controller with a 2 KB subscriber budget, so on a loaded runner the controller itself fell behind (SLOW_CONSUMER) and lost control until it reattached; its next write met CONTROL_REQUIRED, and the un-awaited reader rejected with 'Terminal ended' after teardown. Fixed by task/ci-flakes: the controller writes the lines at once, and the reader's rejection is caught until it's awaited.
